metadata.title: Claude, Customize.
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Teardown register: does Claude, customize mean Claude changes itself? Take the skill apart, explain the actual machinery — a folder plus a SKILL.md, read then executed — and judge the design choice: same spec in, same shaped output out, silent outside that scope.
metadata.one_flag: N/A — every claim is a confirmed, present-tense description of how a Claude Skill works, not an inference

beats.narration_text: I'm Liam, in for Bear. Someone asked whether Claude, customize means Claude changes itself. Not quite — the skill shapes one task's output to a spec in a file, every time. Nothing outside that spec moves. Here's what's actually happening.

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types the naive framing, hesitates on 'ITSELF', corrects to 'output', lands the real question

props.text:
Can Claude customize
ITSELF for
me?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter). Writer types the wrong-guess 'ITSELF' (Claude rewires itself), hesitates, corrects to 'output' — narration frames the same misread in Teardown voice and Liam introduces himself in for Bear (IN-FOR-BEAR LAW). TIMING LAW: ≥9s typing window is covered by the ~16s narration + lead_silence_s 0.8.

beats.narration_text: Here's what a skill actually is — a folder Claude reads before it works. This one is customize. The SKILL.md file inside holds the whole instruction set in plain English — no hidden logic, no compiled binary. Claude reads it, then acts on it. The file is the program. They optimized for legibility: you can read the same file Claude reads.

props.title: A skill is a folder.
props.calloutText: The SKILL.md is the instruction set.

beats.narration_text: The pipeline lives in the Steps section. Claude reads each step in order, then runs it. Straight-line execution — no branching unless a step spells it out. They optimized for predictability over cleverness. You always know what happens next.

Here's the interesting constraint. Shape this one task's output to what the file specifies — nothing more. Stay inside that scope and the output holds its shape, every time. Ask for anything the file doesn't cover, and the skill has nothing to say. That's the trade-off — same shape, in exchange for narrow scope. Reliable within its boundary, silent outside it.

props.heading: The interesting constraint.
props.body: One task's output, shaped to the file's spec — nothing more.
props.sparkLine: Reliable within its boundary. Silent outside it.

beats.narration_text: So here's the carry-out. Same spec in, same shaped output out, every time. Anything the file doesn't cover, Claude has no opinion about. That's the whole design — a narrow, reliable shape instead of a wide, unpredictable one.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's a prompt you can paste directly into Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini. Ask it: I want to understand how Claude Skills actually work — a Skill is a folder with a SKILL.md file that tells Claude how to shape one specific task's output. Design me a small SKILL.md for a task I care about — say, formatting my daily standup notes as a three-line status update. Include a name, a one-line description, a numbered steps section, and one example of the shaped output. Then explain what would break if I removed the steps section. Go deeper: pick a task where you don't want a fixed output shape — one where you want Claude to surprise you. Explain why a Skill is the wrong tool there, and what pattern would fit instead.
